questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If scientists had discovered the vaccine sooner, thousands wouldn't be suffering now.
If scientists discovered the vaccine sooner, thousands wouldn't be suffering now.
If scientists had discovered the vaccine sooner, thousands wouldn't have suffered now.
If scientists had discovered the vaccine sooner, thousands won't suffer now.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: If + past perfect (past condition), would + base verb (present result): 'If scientists had discovered..., thousands wouldn't be suffering now.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Research funding will keep declining unless governments won't invest more.
Research funding will keep declining unless governments invest more.
Research funding will keep declining unless that governments invest more.
Research funding will keep declining without governments invest more.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if...not' and is followed by an affirmative clause: 'unless governments invest more.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Several groundbreaking discoveries has been made this year.
Several groundbreaking discoveries have made this year.
Several groundbreaking discoveries have been made this year.
Several groundbreaking discoveries have being made this year.
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: have/has been + past participle: 'have been made this year.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This experimental technology should tested immediately.
This experimental technology should being tested immediately.
This experimental technology should be test immediately.
This experimental technology should be tested immediately.
questions.explanation: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle: 'should be tested immediately.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "Please follow the safety protocol.")
options: The scientist told us to follow the safety protocol.
The scientist told us follow the safety protocol.
The scientist said us to follow the safety protocol.
The scientist told us that follow the safety protocol.
questions.explanation: Reported commands: tell + object + to + base verb: 'told us to follow the safety protocol.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "You should replicate the experiment.")
options: She suggested to replicate the experiment.
She suggested replicating the experiment.
She suggested me replicating the experiment.
She suggested that I replicating the experiment.
questions.explanation: 'Suggest' is followed by a gerund or 'that + subject + base verb': 'suggested replicating the experiment.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The laboratory which she works for it researches renewable materials.
The laboratory for that she works researches renewable materials.
The laboratory for which she works researches renewable materials.
The laboratory she works for which researches renewable materials.
questions.explanation: In formal style, the preposition moves before 'which': 'the laboratory for which she works.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The study publishing last week revealed a breakthrough in battery technology.
The study published last week reveal a breakthrough in battery technology.
The study which published last week revealed a breakthrough in battery technology.
The study published last week revealed a breakthrough in battery technology.
questions.explanation: A passive meaning reduces 'which was published' to the past participle alone: 'The study published last week...'

questions.topic: Modal verbs of past deduction (must have)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The researchers must have overlooked a key variable.
The researchers must overlooked a key variable.
The researchers must have overlook a key variable.
The researchers must has overlooked a key variable.
questions.explanation: Past deduction: must have + past participle: 'must have overlooked a key variable.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The lab should acted sooner to publish its findings.
The lab should have acted sooner to publish its findings.
The lab should have act sooner to publish its findings.
The lab should has acted sooner to publish its findings.
questions.explanation: Past regret/criticism: should have + past participle: 'should have acted sooner.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Computing power rose dramatically over the past two decades.
Computing power has risen dramatically over the past two decades.
Computing power have risen dramatically over the past two decades.
Computing power have rose dramatically over the past two decades.
questions.explanation: 'Over the past two decades' links the past to the present, so present perfect is used: 'has risen dramatically.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: By the time the results were published, another team confirmed the finding.
By the time the results had published, another team confirmed the finding.
By the time the results were published, another team have already confirmed the finding.
By the time the results were published, another team had already confirmed the finding.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect: 'another team had already confirmed the finding.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Scientists are meeting next week to discuss the new findings.
Scientists meet next week to discuss the new findings.
Scientists will meeting next week to discuss the new findings.
Scientists are meet next week to discuss the new findings.
questions.explanation: Present continuous expresses a fixed future arrangement: 'are meeting next week.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She said she will publish the findings next month.
She said she would publish the findings next month.
She said she would published the findings next month.
She said she would have publish the findings next month.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'will' shifts back to 'would': 'she said she would publish the findings.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish governments take scientific research more seriously.
I wish governments have taken scientific research more seriously.
I wish governments took scientific research more seriously.
I wish governments would take scientific research more seriously as a policy.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past simple expresses regret about a present situation: 'I wish governments took scientific research more seriously.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish the team warned us earlier about the risks.
I wish the team have warned us earlier about the risks.
I wish the team would have warned us earlier about the risks.
I wish the team had warned us earlier about the risks.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past perfect expresses regret about the past: 'I wish the team had warned us earlier.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We had our prototype tested by an independent lab.
We had tested our prototype by an independent lab.
We had our prototype test by an independent lab.
We have our prototype tested by an independent lab last year.
questions.explanation: Causative form: have + object + past participle shows someone else did the action: 'had our prototype tested.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Never before the field had seen such rapid progress.
Never before had the field seen such rapid progress.
Never before did the field seen such rapid progress.
Never before has the field had seen such rapid progress.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbials at the start trigger inversion: 'Never before had the field seen...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The team is looking the anomaly into.
The team is looking in to the anomaly.
The team is looking into the anomaly.
The team is looking into to the anomaly.
questions.explanation: 'Look into' means 'investigate' and is inseparable: 'looking into the anomaly.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: What the field urgently need are more diverse funding sources.
That the field urgently needs is more diverse funding sources.
What the field urgently needs is more diverse funding sources it.
What the field urgently needs is more diverse funding sources.
questions.explanation: 'What' clefts take a singular verb when the complement is singular: 'What the field needs is more diverse funding.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Some labs share their data openly, whereas others keep it confidential.
Some labs share their data openly, whereas others keeps it confidential.
Some labs share their data openly whereas, others keep it confidential.
Some labs share their data openly despite others keep it confidential.
questions.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two clauses and is followed directly by the subject: 'whereas others keep it confidential.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: In spite the setbacks, the project succeeded.
In spite of the setbacks, the project succeeded.
Despite of the setbacks, the project succeeded.
In spite of the setbacks, the project succeeded though.
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' is followed by a noun phrase: 'In spite of the setbacks, the project succeeded.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: A number of studies has linked AI research to job displacement.
The number of studies have linked AI research to job displacement.
A number of studies have linked AI research to job displacement.
A great number of studies has linked AI research to job displacement.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb: 'a number of studies have linked...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She spoke in behalf of the entire research team.
She spoke on behalf for the entire research team.
She spoke behalf of the entire research team.
She spoke on behalf of the entire research team.
questions.explanation: 'On behalf of' means 'representing someone': 'she spoke on behalf of the research team.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The development of new materials accelerated innovation significantly.
The develop of new materials accelerated innovation significantly.
The developing of new materials accelerated innovation significantly.
The development of new materials accelerate innovation significantly.
questions.explanation: Formal writing often nominalizes verbs into nouns: 'develop' becomes 'the development of...'

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate formal opening line for an email requesting information about a research grant?
options: I'm writing to ask you about the research grant, ok?
I am writing to enquire about the eligibility criteria for your research grant.
Just wanted to know about the grant.
Hey, tell me about the grant.
questions.explanation: 'I am writing to enquire about...' is a standard formal opening for information requests.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate opening line for a formal complaint about plagiarized research?
options: I'm writing because I'm really mad about the plagiarism.
I want to complain about the plagiarism, it's bad.
I am writing to express my concern about suspected plagiarism in a recent paper.
I am writing to express my concern about suspected plagiarism in a recent paper, ok.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use measured language such as 'I am writing to express my concern about...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The results of the clinical trial were extreme alarming.
The results of the clinical trial were extremely alarm.
The results of the clinical trial were very much alarming.
The results of the clinical trial were extremely alarming.
questions.explanation: 'Extremely' (adverb) modifies the adjective 'alarming': 'were extremely alarming.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The new material is lighter. Moreover, it is more durable.
The new material is lighter, moreover it is more durable.
The new material is lighter. Moreover it is more durable.
The new material is lighter moreover, it is more durable.
questions.explanation: 'Moreover' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma: 'The new material is lighter. Moreover, it is more durable.'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You'd support more funding for research, didn't you?
You'd support more funding for research, wouldn't you?
You'd support more funding for research, would you?
You'd support more funding for research, wouldn't it?
questions.explanation: A positive statement with 'would' takes a negative tag: 'You'd support..., wouldn't you?'
